output.methodChoice: EDF-2 with evidence limited to E1-E5 plus X10 and X5
output.brief:
Most likely, store 14's rise is mainly a measurement artifact, not a confirmed increase in losses. Its shrink figures for Q1–Q3 are interim estimates from rotating cycle counts, which the AP analytics memo puts at roughly ±0.6 points per quarter. Across 114 store-years, about half of the two-quarter rises were not confirmed by the year-end full count, and store 14's full-count shrink was flat for FY2023–FY2025. Department shares were stable, which argues against a mix shift. The night-stocker tip was checked on CCTV and the bale runs were routine. Recorded shoplifting incidents rose chain-wide after the new app launched while chain shrink stayed flat, so incident counts do not show a real loss increase. I am moderately confident (about 65–70%) in this. The self-checkout and staff-theft explanations are not resolved by the evidence I reviewed.

Next steps: keep store 14 in the 7 December full physical count and reply to Regional Operations before 20 November declining the roll-forward. Do not suspend the named employee or buy a door guard yet. Compare the full-count result with the interim figure before deciding on store-specific spending. Reviewing self-checkout data separately is still reasonable.
